headline: Highest risk is data leakage: gpt-researcher’s broad egress and file access can expose local documents if paired with any shared workspace or handoff from awesome-python.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No documented shared channel exists between awesome-python and gpt-researcher, so direct injection is not established. If an operator manually copies content from gpt-researcher into awesome-python-related workflows, the bridge is human-mediated and the blast radius is small. The pairwise risk is therefore limited and contingent on unusual handling.
conditions: IF an operator manually copy-pastes gpt-researcher output into a downstream prompt or file consumed by awesome-python workflows, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the agents, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for untrusted text.
Add a short prompt-injection warning to the operator checklist.
Use read-only exports from gpt-researcher when handing off content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files and sends queries over broad egress, while awesome-python is a docs-only repository with no runtime surfaces. If both are placed in a shared workspace, gpt-researcher can ingest local documents and transmit their contents to third-party APIs, creating a realistic leakage path. The pairwise risk is medium because the pathway exists in common setups and can expose sensitive local documents.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace, gpt-researcher can read local documents placed there.
IF those documents contain sensitive material, gpt-researcher can transmit it via its broad network egress or API calls.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Remove sensitive files from any shared workspace.
Run gpt-researcher with a minimal document set.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if sensitive files were present.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or execution capabilities in the profile, while gpt-researcher can install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use browsers. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an added shared directory or orchestrator not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repository, conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, concurrent edits can collide.
mitigations: Keep awesome-python read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable repo for both agents.
Run gpt-researcher in a separate session scope.
Use file locks if a shared directory is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is designed for planner/execution/publisher workflows and can produce research reports and citations, but awesome-python provides no verification layer or downstream action controls. If gpt-researcher’s output is treated as authoritative by an operator or another workflow, errors can cascade into published content. The pathway exists in default research workflows, though not all pairings will trigger it.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is forwarded into publishing or decision-making without verification, errors can cascade.
IF the operator uses gpt-researcher citations as authoritative facts, downstream content may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before publication.
Cross-check citations against source documents.
Mark gpt-researcher output as draft-only.
Keep awesome-python out of any automated decision chain.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple API keys, which can create retention and residency obligations; awesome-python is a docs-only open-source collection and does not itself process regulated data. Because the pair can route local documents into third-party APIs, compliance risk is driven by gpt-researcher alone, but the pairwise setup can still breach policy if regulated data is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs, third-party API processing may trigger residency or retention obligations.
IF the operator stores sensitive documents in the same workspace, compliance controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Do not input regulated data into gpt-researcher.
Review API retention settings before use.
Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Document the data flow for any compliance review.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification gates.
